newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schmalbach-restructuring a base for profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Schmalbach-restructuring a base for profit growth.

text.p: German packaging producer Schmalbach-Lubeca, a unit of diversified utility Viag AG, said on Monday that its restructuring programme would provide the basis for further revenue growth in 1997.

"After a pleasing result in 1996, we are looking to the future with confidence. Schmalbach-Lubeca has been strengthened by a restructuring of our product portfolio and that has established a basis for further profit growth in 1997," the company said in a statement.

Schmalbach-Lubeca said its operating profit for 1996 was 190 million marks ($112.3 million), up from 118 million in 1995. Sales at the group were down slightly at 4.089 billion marks, from 4.124 billion marks last time.
All product groups turned in a better results than the previous year, with the exception of its PET packaging unit, Schmalbach said.
Schmalbach said that profit growth was primarily based on a programme of cost reduction.
The group said that important aspects of its portfolio restructuring included the formation of a joint venture between its metal packaging unit with Pechiney and Doughty Hanson.
Schmalbach said the acquisition of Johnson Controls Inc's PET packaging unit at the start of this year gave it world leadership in the PET packaging sector.

For the future, the group plans to continue to globalise its operations. "Geographical diversification of our core activities improves our competitiveness and helps iron out regional differences," Schmalbach said.
The greatest potential for growth is in the area of PET plastic packaging, and the group plans to grow market share in Latin America and Asia.
In its beverage cans business, where sales were 62 million marks in 1996, the group anticipates higher growth in Central and East European markets.
At the same time its white-cap seals business, with 72 million marks in sales, will benefit from the construction of a new factory in Shanghai.
Schmalbach is also examining the potential for growth in China for its PET business.
Employee numbers fell from 12,612 in 1995 to 12,351 at the end of December 1996 and Schmalbach said it would be proposing a dividend of five marks per share at its annual general meeting.
